history.summary: Dry-run mutation, non-transactional rollback, incomplete new-project output, hidden analysis errors, unusable GUI preview, duplicated installer logic, ineffective rigor overrides, and incomplete final validation.
Receipt reuse ignored directory/configuration drift, tampered directory metadata could delete user content, and GUI guard/target identity state became stale.
Rollback fault recovery left receipts non-retryable, editable directory provenance could delete user content, one missing receipt field leaked a traceback, and GUI controls overlapped.
All prior failures passed, but a self-consistently forged created-file receipt could still delete unrelated user content.

Deletion-free rollback passed, but latest receipt selection was non-chronological, editable created entries were misreported as provenance, incomplete merge evidence claimed success, and GUI hid preserved paths.

Typed receipt centralization passed, but no-argument rollback skipped newer completed receipts, timestamp fields could disagree, and editable omitted-merge evidence still produced false complete status.

Ordinary latest-state rules passed, but receipt status was not integrity-bound, disabled recorded configuration could hide live omitted merge evidence, and lifecycle timestamps allowed impossible ordering.
Authenticated receipt state passed, but hardlinked keys, symlinked/insecure ancestor directories, and tests using the ambient per-user signing key violated the trust boundary.
Descriptor-backed key handling still allowed hardlink/race exposure and the user replaced automatic rollback with a simpler manual restoration requirement.
